- Short answers for: tenant isolation model, control-plane access, KMS boundary, and audit log retention.

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact diagram and a short narrative draft below that you can paste into your questionnaire.

Attachment (attached): inference-fabric-v1.pdf (single-page diagram)

Narrative (short answers you requested):
1) Tenant isolation model: Dedicated — customer workloads run in a reserved GPU pool and logically isolated VPCs; Private — customer control plane is deployed into a customer VPC/air-gapped environment. In both modes we enforce strict tenant fencing via network ACLs, per-tenant routing, and per-instance identity.

2) Control-plane access: Control plane operations for Hosted/Dedicated run in Redwood-managed control plane; for Private deployments, control plane endpoints are customer-facing and configured to accept connections only from customer-managed bastion or peered admin networks. Administrative access to control plane services is authenticated via SSO + short-lived certs; RBAC is enforced at service and API gateway layers (see CAIQ mapping in attachment).

3) KMS boundary: Customer-managed keys are supported for Private deployments (BYOK) and Dedicated where requested; default Hosted keys are managed by Redwood KMS with separate key rings per customer. Keys are never exported in plaintext and are accessed via HSM-backed KMS APIs with least privilege.

4) Audit logs and retention: We stream control-plane audit logs to an isolated logging bucket per customer (or to customer-managed SIEM for Private). Retention and export policies are configurable; default retention for SOC2 evidence is 13 months.

5) Shared GPU side-channel mitigations: We recommend Dedicated (reserved pools) for highest isolation. Runtime mitigations include per-VM scheduling, kernel page-table isolation where relevant, and no co-scheduling across tenants on the same CUDA context; for Private deployments, customers can run on physically isolated hardware.

I'll leave the SIG/CAIQ matrix to Kimberly and Dev to attach — tagging them for the mapping and the segregation matrix CSV. Let us know if you want this as a short memorandum or a slide.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — answers inline and an exportable attestation at the bottom.

1) Physical co-hosting of GPUs in Dedicated pools: By default Dedicated uses reserved clusters where we do not place two unrelated customers on the same CUDA instance. Our scheduler enforces tenancy isolation such that different tenants are not co-scheduled on the same GPU context. For customers requiring absolute physical separation we offer a physically isolated host option (no multi-tenant hardware). See segregation-matrix.csv row "gpu_co_hosting".

2) Per-tenant KMS key rings: Per-tenant (isolated) key rings are available as a standard option for Dedicated when requested during provisioning. For Hosted customers we provide per-tenant key ring namespaces by default; BYOK (customer-managed keys) is an opt-in feature for Dedicated and packaged by default for Private deployments. See sig-caiq-mapping.xlsx tab "KMS".

3) Private control plane packaging: The Private offering includes a control plane package that can be deployed into a customer VPC (containerized Helm charts / operator) or run as a peered management plane depending on the customer's network policy. We provide both deployment artifacts and an operator-run option; deployment choice is recorded in the onboarding runbook.

Exportable attestation (one paragraph you can paste):
"Redwood Inference provides tenant isolation through a combination of reserved compute pools, per-tenant network segmentation, and auditable control-plane access. Dedicated customers may request physically isolated hosts; per-tenant KMS namespaces and customer-managed key options are available. Audit logs and telemetry are stored per-tenant and can be exported to customer-managed storage. These assertions map to the referenced SIG/CAIQ control IDs in the attached mapping. For detailed configuration artifacts, see the attached segregation matrix and SIG/CAIQ mapping spreadsheet."

Attachments included in this message: inference-fabric-v1.pdf, segregation-matrix.csv, sig-caiq-mapping.xlsx

If you want I can also provide a one-page slide with the same language and the diagram for Procurement.

Best regards,
